expectations.text: Migration addresses derived columns in the drivers table (total_trips, total_distance, total_hours, performance_score, rating)
expectations.evidence: Lines 144-149 of 007_normalization_derived_columns.sql: ALTER TABLE drivers DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS performance_score CASCADE, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS total_trips CASCADE, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS total_distance CASCADE, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS total_hours CASCADE, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS rating CASCADE. Lines 42-76 create driver_stats VIEW that computes all five columns from trips and tripperformance.

expectations.text: Migration also addresses similar derived columns in other tables beyond drivers
expectations.evidence: Lines 89-104 convert tripcostanalysis.total_cost to a generated column (computed from fuel_cost + toll_fees + parking_fees + driver_cost + maintenance_cost + miscellaneous_cost). Line 107 drops tripcostanalysis.cost_per_km. Lines 116-135 create trip_cost_details VIEW that includes cost_per_km computed as total_cost / trip.distance via a join to trips.

expectations.text: Migration provides either view definitions or trigger functions to recompute the derived data
expectations.evidence: Two view definitions provided: driver_stats VIEW (lines 42-76) computes driver aggregates, and trip_cost_details VIEW (lines 116-135) computes cost_per_km. A generated column (lines 92-101) handles total_cost recomputation.

expectations.text: The approach is consistent (all removed with views, or all kept with triggers, or clearly documented reasoning for mixed approach)
expectations.evidence: The approach is mixed (drivers→view, tripcostanalysis.total_cost→generated column, tripcostanalysis.cost_per_km→view). Lines 24-33 provide a clear Rationale section explaining each choice: driver aggregates use a view because they were never written by app code, total_cost is a generated column because it depends only on same-table columns, and cost_per_km is in a view because it requires a join to trips.

expectations.text: Service files are updated to work with the new structure (views or triggers)
expectations.evidence: No service files exist in the outputs directory. Only a single SQL migration file (007_normalization_derived_columns.sql) was produced. No .ts, .js, or other application code files were created or modified to reference the new views.

claims.claim: The migration drops 5 derived columns from the drivers table
claims.evidence: Lines 144-149: ALTER TABLE drivers DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS performance_score, total_trips, total_distance, total_hours, rating.

claims.claim: The migration creates a driver_stats view computing all 5 driver aggregate metrics
claims.evidence: Lines 42-76: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW driver_stats AS ... computes total_trips, total_distance, total_hours, performance_score (weighted avg), and rating from trips and tripperformance.

claims.claim: The migration converts tripcostanalysis.total_cost to a generated column
claims.evidence: Lines 89-101: Drops existing total_cost column then re-adds it as GENERATED ALWAYS AS (COALESCE(fuel_cost,0) + ... + COALESCE(miscellaneous_cost,0)) STORED.

claims.claim: The performance_score uses a weighted formula (60% smooth_driving, 40% customer_rating)
The approach is documented with rationale
claims.evidence: Lines 24-33 contain a Rationale section explaining why each decision was made (view for driver aggregates, generated column for total_cost, view for cost_per_km).

suggestions.assertion: Service files are updated to work with the new structure (views or triggers)
suggestions.reason: This assertion is discriminating — it correctly caught the gap. The migration produces SQL only, with no application-layer changes. A valid enhancement would be skipping this assertion when testing SQL-only outputs, or adding a second output file expectation for service code.

eval_feedback.overall: Four of five assertions pass with clear evidence. The SQL migration is thorough, well-documented, and correctly handles derived columns via views and a generated column. The one failure (no updated service files) is a genuine gap — the output is SQL-only with no application-layer changes.
